Supervised assessment.scope: Assessment completed under supervision with AI access controlled: in-person invigilated exams, in-class tests and supervised lab tests.
Supervised assessment.includes: Paper or computer-based exams in an invigilated room; supervised lab tests on controlled machines.
Supervised assessment.excludes: Online or remotely proctored exams and lockdown browsers (treated as weaker variants and named as exceptions, rule C1); vivas (Oral assessments); live demos of the student's own work (Practical demonstrations).

Unsupervised formats.scope: Work completed without supervision, where AI use cannot be controlled: take-home programming tasks, take-home lab work, assignments, reports, projects and online quizzes.
Unsupervised formats.includes: Take-home lab exercises and notebooks, coursework, capstone and group projects, essays and reports, unsupervised online quizzes.
Unsupervised formats.excludes: Any supervised or live verification added to the task (rated under its own type).

Oral assessments.scope: Live spoken questioning of the individual student about their knowledge or their own work: vivas, interactive orals, oral defences and code-explanation interviews.
Oral assessments.includes: In-person or real-time online vivas with unscripted follow-up questions; short sampled oral checks.
Oral assessments.excludes: Pre-recorded or scripted presentations (more exposed; named as exceptions); written reflections.

Practical demonstrations.scope: A live demonstration of working skill to an assessor, in person or in real time online, with unscripted questions or change requests: live coding, lab checkoffs, prototype demonstrations, modifying code on request.
Practical demonstrations.includes: TA checkoffs, live coding tasks, supervised live demos of a project or prototype.
Practical demonstrations.excludes: Recorded demos and screencasts made without an assessor present (treated as a variant of Process evidence and named as exceptions); take-home lab work (Unsupervised formats).

Staged submissions.scope: A task split into assessed stages with feedback between them: checkpoints, milestones, drafts and multi-stage projects.
Staged submissions.includes: Proposal, design, implementation and final stages; draft and revision cycles; milestone reviews.
Staged submissions.excludes: The verification method used at a checkpoint (for example a viva at a milestone is rated under Oral assessments).

Process evidence.scope: Records of how the work was produced, submitted or captured for assessment: version-control histories, development logs, prompt and chat histories, reflective journals, activity logs and recorded screencasts or walkthroughs.
Process evidence.includes: Git commit histories, student-kept logs, system-captured editor or keystroke logs, AI chat logs, recorded demos without an assessor present.
Process evidence.excludes: Live questioning about the process (Oral assessments or Practical demonstrations).

Personalised tasks.scope: Tasks individualised or contextualised to the student, course or local setting, including designs intended to be AI-resistant.
Personalised tasks.includes: Individual topics or datasets, local case studies, course-specific commands or constraints, varied question instances.
Personalised tasks.excludes: Generic tasks with only cosmetic variation.

AI-use declarations.scope: Requirements for students to disclose and account for their GenAI use: declarations, disclosure statements, AI-use scales (e.g. AIAS), reflections on AI use and critique of AI output.
AI-use declarations.includes: Declaration forms, prompt and output appendices, AI-use reflections, tasks that require critique or correction of AI output.
AI-use declarations.excludes: System-captured logs of AI use (Process evidence).
